newsitem.title: CHILE: Four killed in Chilean copper mine rockslide.
newsitem.headline: Four killed in Chilean copper mine rockslide.

text.p: A rockslide at a Chilean copper mine killed four workers on Wednesday, burying them under tons of earth and boulders in the third fatal mining accident in Chile this week, officials and mine spokesmen said.

Workers at the El Abra copper mine in arid northern Chile were doing routine work on a conveyor belt stretching from the mine to a nearby ore crushing plant when they were buried by the rockslide, spokesmen said.
The bodies of all four workers were recovered after being trapped for hours under tons of rubble.
"They have found all four bodies," said El Loa province governor Jose Ayala by telephone from the nearby city of Calama.

The mine, built by U.S. mining company Cyprus Amax Minerals in a joint venture with Chile's state copper firm Codelco, opened in August and is set to become one of Chile's largest mines with annual production of 225,000 tons.

The accident was cutting production at the mine about 900 miles (1,500 km) north of Santiago, though spokesmen said it was unknown by how much. They did not know if the conveyor belt had been covered in the rockslide.
The seven-mile (11 km) long belt, the mine's lifeline, passes through a narrow, rocky gorge during parts of its path from the open pit mine to the crusher plant.
The accident added to an unusual rash of mining accidents in Chile this week.

On Sunday, a worker died at Codelco's El Teniente mine when he tumbled down a 19-yard (19-meter) pit, and another miner died at Codelco's Andina mine two days later when he was hit in the head by a swinging steel door. Production was not affected in either of those accidents.
